The architecture enforces a strict separation between internal computation and customer-facing outputs via the certification gate. Capture begins immediately upon signal availability, enabling asynchronous logging without blocking. Build processes run concurrently unless dependencies are proven real, ensuring scalability. The failure mode arises when internal systems are not wired into a closed-loop learning system, preventing model improvement. The ledger rule prevents unauthorized edits, maintaining ownership integrity. The founder's authority resolves disputes over row ownership, ensuring accountability. The core insight is that while we can build anything, only certified outputs reach customers—this creates a dualism between engineering capability and operational constraint.
